title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Rules on Judicial Police Security for Criminal Trials in People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the

Rules on Judicial Police Service Security for Criminal Trials of

People's Courts

Fa Fa [2009] No. 46

To the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Supreme People's Court's Rules on Judicial Police Service Security for Criminal Trials of People's Courts are hereby issued to you for your earnest implementation.

July 30, 2009

Rules on Judicial Police Service Security for Criminal Trials of People's Courts

I. General Provisions

Article 1 These Rules are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Police Law of the People's Republic of China, the Rules of the People's Courts on Court Trials of the People's Republic of China, the Interim Regulations on Judicial Police of People's Courts, and other relevant laws and administrative regulations, for the purpose of regulating the service security work for criminal trials conducted by judicial police of People's Courts (hereinafter referred to as judicial police).

Article 2 Criminal trial service security (hereinafter referred to as service security) refers to the official acts performed by judicial police in accordance with the law to ensure the smooth progress of the criminal trial work of People's Courts.

The service security referred to in these Rules includes: maintaining trial order and guarding court security in criminal trial work; protecting the personal safety of adjudicators, prosecutors, defense counsel, and other participants in the proceedings; preventing and stopping illegal and criminal acts that hinder criminal trial activities; lawfully escorting and guarding defendants and criminals; lawfully conducting security checks on observers; summoning witnesses and expert witnesses, and transmitting and presenting evidence.

Article 3 Judicial police, when performing service security duties, shall: strictly abide by the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, strictly, civilly, and normatively enforce the law; keep trial secrets and work secrets; wear uniforms as required, maintain a neat appearance and dignified demeanor; and hold valid identification documents such as police officer cards.

Judicial police on court duty shall, in court trial activities, lawfully perform their duties in accordance with the instructions of the presiding judge or the sole judge.

Article 4 When deploying and using police instruments and weapons in the course of performing service security duties, judicial police must comply with the relevant provisions of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Use of Police Instruments and Weapons by the People's Police.

II. Organization and Command

Article 5 In service security work, the judicial police department shall arrange and deploy police forces based on the nature of the case, the number of defendants, and the method of trial; and shall equip vehicles, weapons, and police instruments.

Police forces shall be deployed in accordance with regulations. Based on service security requirements, separate units (groups) for escort, guarding, court duty, security checks, and emergency response shall be established.

Command vehicles and prison vans shall be equipped, and backup vehicles shall be equipped when necessary.

Weapons and police instruments shall be equipped.

Before performing service security duties, vehicles, weapons, and police instruments shall be maintained and inspected to ensure they are in a serviceable condition.

Article 6 The facilities of trial courts and detention premises shall be inspected. Facilities and items that hinder service security work shall be modified or removed.

Article 7 For service security work involving a large number of defendants or other major criminal cases, the judicial police department shall formulate a "Service Security Implementation Plan." The implementation plan shall cover contents such as organization and command, deployment of police forces, and "Emergency Response Plan for Unexpected Incidents."

Article 8 Where there is a shortage of police forces in service security work, the Interim Rules on the Transfer and Use of Judicial Police by People's Courts shall apply.

Article 9 The judicial police corps of each Higher People's Court shall be responsible for the service security work for second-instance trials of death penalty cases and shall uniformly organize and coordinate the deployment and arrangement of police forces. For second-instance death penalty cases where the Supreme People's Court or a Higher People's Court needs to try the case at the court where the defendant is detained or to interrogate the defendant, the service security shall, in principle, be provided by the judicial police department of the court at the defendant's place of detention.

III. Implementation Requirements

Article 10 The judicial police department shall promptly provide service security in accordance with the needs of the criminal trial work of the People's Court to which it belongs.

Article 11 For service security involving a large number of defendants or other major criminal cases, the criminal trial department requesting the use of judicial police for service security shall submit an application for police services to the judicial police department at least three working days before the police service is needed.

The application for police services shall include information such as the requesting department, the time of police service, the nature of the case, the number of defendants, and the condition of observers.

Article 12 After receiving the task, the judicial police department shall carefully review whether the custody transfer procedures and the relevant information provided by the requesting department are complete. If the procedures or information are incomplete or erroneous, it may request the requesting department to make corrections.

Article 13 After judicial police performing escort duties arrive at the detention center or the place where the defendant is detained, they shall go through the custody transfer procedures in accordance with regulations. When escorting the defendant out of the detention area, they shall check each defendant's identity and the cause of the case against the custody transfer warrant one by one, and shall frisk the defendant to prevent them from carrying dangerous or contraband items.

Restraints shall be applied to defendants. For defendants who may be sentenced to relatively severe punishments such as life imprisonment or the death penalty, leg irons shall be used.

Co-defendants shall be escorted separately by vehicle. If separate vehicle escort is not possible, measures shall be taken to ensure that no collusion occurs. Defendants in major cases shall be escorted in dedicated vehicles.

During escort, judicial police shall closely monitor the defendants to prevent escape, assault, self-harm, self-mutilation, or collusion.

During escort, judicial police shall correctly use police lights and sirens in accordance with regulations and use civil and standard language. Prison vans performing escort duties shall not carry unrelated persons.

Article 14 After escorting defendants to the detention room or temporary detention premises, the judicial police performing escort duties and those performing guarding duties shall go through handover procedures. The judicial police on guard duty shall check the number, identity, and cause of the case of the defendants, and understand and grasp the defendants' physical condition and emotional state.

The time of entry and exit of defendants into and out of the detention room, the names of defendants, the number of defendants, and the names of the escorting judicial police shall be registered one by one, and the guard records shall be carefully filled out.

Guarding judicial police shall use notification statements to inform defendants of the rules and discipline they must comply with during detention, and shall also inform defendants of their rights.

Co-defendants, adult defendants and minor defendants, and male defendants and female defendants shall be detained separately. Defendants in major cases shall be detained separately.

During the guard period, restraints on defendants may be removed. However, for defendants who may be sentenced to relatively severe punishments such as life imprisonment or the death penalty, or who show signs of possible escape, assault, suicide, or self-mutilation, restraints shall not be removed.

Guarding judicial police shall frequently patrol the guard premises, closely monitor the activities of defendants, and prevent accidents. Enhanced guard measures shall be taken for defendants in major cases.

Article 15 Judicial police on court duty shall enter the court before the start of court trial activities and determine their positions for guarding the court.

Judicial police on court duty shall discourage and stop persons who violate court rules. For persons who do not comply with such discouragement and cessation, judicial police on court duty shall, under the instructions of the presiding judge or the sole judge, take compulsory measures in accordance with the law to stop their illegal acts or forcibly remove them from the court.

For persons who seriously disrupt court order, judicial police on court duty shall take compulsory measures in accordance with the law to control them; if a fine or detention is imposed upon approval by the president, the judicial police shall execute it.

Under the instructions of the presiding judge or the sole judge, judicial police on court duty shall be responsible for summoning witnesses and expert witnesses, and transmitting and presenting evidence; they shall guide witnesses and expert witnesses into and out of the court, and protect the personal safety of witnesses and expert witnesses in court.

Article 16 Judicial police responsible for escorting defendants in court shall, under the instructions of the presiding judge or the sole judge, escort defendants into and out of the court. During the court trial activities, they shall closely monitor the defendants and keep them within control at all times.

Without approval, victims and their relatives, relatives of defendants, and other unrelated persons are strictly prohibited from approaching defendants.

In court trial activities, restraints shall be removed for defendants. However, for defendants who may be sentenced to relatively severe punishments such as life imprisonment or the death penalty, or who show signs of possible escape, assault, suicide, or self-mutilation, restraints may not be removed.

Article 17 After the trial activities conclude, judicial police shall promptly return the defendants to the detention center or detention premises. Generally, defendants shall not be allowed to read the trial transcripts in the court or the detention room.

Upon approval, defendants may sign for the receipt of the judgment or ruling in the detention room.

IV. Handling of Special Circumstances

Article 18 Where an emergency situation occurs during service security work, judicial police must decisively handle it. After the danger is eliminated, they shall immediately report to or request instructions from the leader of the judicial police department or the presiding judge or the sole judge, and take further measures based on orders or instructions.

Article 19 Under any of the following circumstances during service security work, if a warning proves ineffective, judicial police may use police instruments in accordance with the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Use of Police Instruments and Weapons by the People's Police:

(1) The defendant or criminal escapes;
(2) The defendant, criminal, or other persons attempt to assault adjudicators, prosecutors, defense counsel, or other participants in the proceedings;
(3) Surrounding or attacking judicial police performing service security duties;
(4) Forcibly crossing the cordon set by judicial police for performing service security duties;
(5) Other acts that endanger court order or the work order of the People's Court and require immediate cessation;
(6) Other circumstances where the use of police instruments is permitted by laws and administrative regulations.

When using police instruments in accordance with the preceding paragraph, judicial police shall do so only to the extent necessary to stop the illegal or criminal conduct. Once the illegal or criminal conduct is stopped, the use of police instruments shall immediately cease.

Article 20 Under any of the following emergency situations during service security work, if a warning proves ineffective, judicial police may use weapons in accordance with the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Use of Police Instruments and Weapons by the People's Police:

(1) The defendant or criminal commits violent acts such as murder or hostage-taking;
(2) The defendant or criminal escapes, and the use of weapons is unavoidable to stop it;
(3) Forcibly seizing or robbing the defendant or criminal;
(4) Robbing or seizing firearms or ammunition, seriously endangering public safety;
(5) Using violent methods to resist or obstruct judicial police from lawfully performing their duties, or violently assaulting judicial police, endangering the life safety of judicial police;
(6) Other circumstances where the use of weapons is permitted by laws and administrative regulations.

When using weapons in accordance with the preceding paragraph, if there is no time to issue a warning or if a warning may lead to more serious harmful consequences, weapons may be used directly.

When using weapons, judicial police shall refrain from using weapons and shall immediately cease using weapons in circumstances where the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Use of Police Instruments and Weapons by the People's Police prohibit the use of weapons or require the immediate cessation of use of weapons.

V. Accountability

Article 21 Where an incident occurs during service security work, such as serious disruption of trial order, causing adverse effects, or the escape of a defendant, under any of the following circumstances, the relevant personnel shall be held accountable in accordance with the law:

(1) Leaving the post without authorization;
(2) Negligence of duty or failure to earnestly perform duties;
(3) Colluding with the defendant or their family members to pass letters or items, or provide tips, resulting in serious consequences;
(4) Failing to take timely measures to handle emergency situations occurring during service security work, resulting in serious consequences;
(5) Violating work discipline or relevant regulations, resulting in a serious incident.

Article 22 Where an incident occurs during service security work, such as serious disruption of trial order, causing adverse effects, or the escape of a defendant, under any of the following circumstances, the leadership of the judicial police department of the relevant People's Court shall be held accountable in accordance with the law:

(1) Failing to formulate a "Service Security Implementation Plan" as required;
(2) The police force of judicial police is insufficient to complete the service security task, yet without reporting to the relevant leader, ordering judicial police to perform service security duties in violation of regulations;
(3) The weapons, vehicles, and police instruments used for service security duties do not meet the needs of the work, yet without reporting to the relevant leader, resulting in a serious incident;
(4) Failing to respond promptly or issuing incorrect commands in response to emergency situations during service security work, resulting in serious consequences;
(5) Other circumstances requiring the accountability of the leadership of the judicial police department.

Article 23 Where an incident occurs during service security work, such as serious disruption of trial order, causing adverse effects, or the escape of a defendant, under any of the following circumstances, the leadership of the relevant People's Court in charge shall be held accountable in accordance with the law:

(1) The facilities and equipment of the court or detention room do not meet the requirements for service security work, and no measures are taken to improve or modify them;
(2) The police force of judicial police is insufficient to complete the service security task, yet ordering the judicial police department to perform service security duties in violation of regulations;
(3) The weapons, vehicles, and police instruments used for service security duties do not meet the needs of the work, and no measures are taken to remedy the situation;
(4) Other circumstances requiring the accountability of the leadership in charge.

Article 24 Where an incident occurs during service security work, disciplinary sanctions shall be imposed on the responsible persons based on the nature and severity of the incident. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

VI. Supplementary Provisions

Article 25 These Rules apply to the criminal trial service security work of People's Courts at all levels.

Article 26 The Supreme People's Court is responsible for the interpretation of these Rules.

Article 27 These Rules shall come into effect on the date of issuance.
